hero.headline: Fort Pierce police arrest driver in hit-and-run that seriously injured 7-year-old in crosswalk
hero.teaser: Fort Pierce police have arrested Demetris Johnson, 34, in connection with a hit-and-run crash at North 25th Street and Avenue M that seriously injured a 7-year-old child crossing in a marked crosswalk.
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police have arrested a 34-year-old driver in connection with a hit-and-run crash that seriously injured a 7-year-old child at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M. Demetris Johnson was arrested Wednesday at 2905 U.S. Highway 1 and faces charges of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and driving while license suspended. Police had been investigating the crash in which an early-2000s gold Mercedes-Benz struck two children in a marked crosswalk before the driver fled the scene.

The crash occurred at approximately 8:55 p.m. on Aug. 1 when two children were crossing the roadway in a marked crosswalk. Police said Johnson struck one of the children. Surveillance video obtained from a nearby business captured the crash and shows Johnson exiting his vehicle to check on the children before returning to his vehicle and fleeing the scene.

Investigators identified the suspect vehicle using available investigative technology and law enforcement databases. These resources also assisted officers in identifying Johnson as the driver, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

The 7-year-old has been released from the hospital and is currently recovering, police said. The investigation remains active and ongoing. Anyone with information on this incident is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477.

cards.headline: Indian River County School District earns 'A' rating for fourth consecutive year
cards.teaser: The Indian River County School District received an A grade for the fourth straight year, with all but one school in the district earning an A rating. Dodgertown Elementary School
cards.body:
The Indian River County School District received an A grade for the fourth straight year, with all but one school in the district earning an A rating. Dodgertown Elementary School was the only school to receive a B rating.

District Superintendent Dr. David Moore said parents can expect a quality education no matter which school they choose in Indian River County. The district maintains its A grade by investing in teachers and staff who have helped improve the district over the past six years. School leaders identify pain points and allocate resources and funding to address those issues and prevent the district from falling in the ratings.

Moore said those efforts are reflected in the number of parents choosing to keep their children in the public school system. The district exceeded the state's projected enrollment for the community for the second straight year due to its willingness to transform the student experience over the last six years.

The School District of Indian River County is ranked in nine out of 12 accountability components. The district says that demonstrates exceptional performance in educating students from the time they begin their education through graduation day.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
The 36 Border Collies rescued from a Palm City home Monday are now receiving medical care, nourishment and grooming as they begin their recovery at the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast. Sarah Fisher, a spokeswoman for the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, said the dogs are very shut down, with some not even walking and just laying on their sides. Veterinary teams are shaving matted fur and examining each dog individually to determine the extent of medical treatment needed.

Fisher described the severity of the animals' condition in detail. We had not only the matted and the underweight and the skin issues, we had glass and metal. We had their tongues were bleeding from them biting their tongues. There was feces in their mouths. Their tails might be falling off. I mean, it's the worst that I've seen, Fisher said. She added that some of the dogs are just laying there and do not know what to do, do not know to lift their head, and do not know how to interact with people, showing they were institutionalized.

The shelter said it could take time before the dogs are ready for foster homes or adoption. The shelter is asking for donations to help cover the cost of caring for the neglected animals, saying the financial burden comes at a time when the shelter was already facing significant challenges. These innocent dogs were inhumanely kept in deplorable conditions, and while they are finally safe, their journey to recovery is just beginning, the shelter said.

cards.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
cards.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
The 36 Border Collies rescued from a Palm City home Monday are now receiving medical care, nourishment and grooming as they begin their recovery at the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast. Sarah Fisher, a spokeswoman for the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, said the dogs are very shut down, with some not even walking and just laying on their sides. Veterinary teams are shaving matted fur and examining each dog individually to determine the extent of medical treatment needed.

Fisher described the severity of the animals' condition in detail. We had not only the matted and the underweight and the skin issues, we had glass and metal. We had their tongues were bleeding from them biting their tongues. There was feces in their mouths. Their tails might be falling off. I mean, it's the worst that I've seen, Fisher said. She added that some of the dogs are just laying there and do not know what to do, do not know to lift their head, and do not know how to interact with people, showing they were institutionalized.

The shelter said it could take time before the dogs are ready for foster homes or adoption. The shelter is asking for donations to help cover the cost of caring for the neglected animals, saying the financial burden comes at a time when the shelter was already facing significant challenges. These innocent dogs were inhumanely kept in deplorable conditions, and while they are finally safe, their journey to recovery is just beginning, the shelter said.

hero.headline: Indian River County School District earns 'A' rating for fourth consecutive year
hero.teaser: The Indian River County School District received an A grade for the fourth straight year, with all but one school in the district earning an A rating. Dodgertown Elementary School
hero.body:
The Indian River County School District received an A grade for the fourth straight year, with all but one school in the district earning an A rating. Dodgertown Elementary School was the only school to receive a B rating.

District Superintendent Dr. David Moore said parents can expect a quality education no matter which school they choose in Indian River County. The district maintains its A grade by investing in teachers and staff who have helped improve the district over the past six years. School leaders identify pain points and allocate resources and funding to address those issues and prevent the district from falling in the ratings.

Moore said those efforts are reflected in the number of parents choosing to keep their children in the public school system. The district exceeded the state's projected enrollment for the community for the second straight year due to its willingness to transform the student experience over the last six years.

The School District of Indian River County is ranked in nine out of 12 accountability components. The district says that demonstrates exceptional performance in educating students from the time they begin their education through graduation day.
